source.title: Whitening and Coloring Batch Transform for GANs
source.authors: Aliaksandr Siarohin; E. Sangineto; N. Sebe

record.file_problem: Text is the full paper, including appendices; no apparent truncation.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 classification error for ResNet-32 and ResNet-56 with BN, WC, and DBN. This is a discriminative test of training error outcomes relevant to V1, though the reported metric is classification error rather than a direct training-error measurement.
record.gate_note: GAN image-generation scores, training-speed plots, and whitening ablations do not measure the claim's classification-training-error outcome. The classification table in Section 6 reports classification error without specifying whether it is training or test error; retain those results as bearing on V1 only with that limitation. Comparisons with cited methods are not extracted as this paper's results.
record.test_reason: The study uses BN and proposes whitening/coloring replacements, reporting their classification and GAN performance. Table 8 does not identify training error, and the training-speed comparisons replace BN with WC rather than compare BN with no normalization. None of V1–V6 is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The authors conclude that WC/cWC can improve image-generation quality and accelerate GAN training across different frameworks and datasets. In classification, WC modestly improves on BN in all four configurations; DBN is slightly better than WC in the two reported CIFAR-10 configurations, with no CIFAR-100 DBN results provided. Appendix F reports an exception to generation improvements for unconditional MNIST.
record.recipe_differences: The claim concerns gradient-based training from random initialization and training classification error; this paper compares normalization methods in classification networks but reports only classification error without identifying it as training error.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported classification error differs by dataset, network depth, and normalization method; the paper says the maximum error difference across tested configurations is below 1%.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 8 reports WC versus BN classification errors of 7.00 versus 7.31 and 6.60 versus 7.21 on CIFAR-10, and 31.25 versus 31.41 and 30.40 versus 30.68 on CIFAR-100. The evaluation split is unspecified.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Replacing first-layer BN with WC modestly reduces reported classification error in the tested ResNets.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 2 reports higher CIFAR-10 Inception Score for WC SN after 20k iterations than for SN after 50k. Both configurations use normalization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: WC can accelerate GAN image-quality improvement relative to BN in the tested setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix E reports collapse to constant gray images in two of three ZCA-whitening runs, while Cholesky-based WC avoided this collapse.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The whitening procedure affects GAN training stability in the tested architecture.

record.problems: The classification comparison is averaged over 5 runs, but no uncertainty estimates are given. The table does not specify whether classification error is training or test error, so it cannot establish the near-zero training-error outcome in V1.
record.rows_left_out: GAN image-generation IS/FID comparisons and plots are outside the classification training-error outcome in the versions. Results for the paper's proposed generator method and its GAN ablations are not rows for these versions.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error, including corrupted/random labels and dependence on capacity or training recipe.
Teacher-student ReLU local minima and the effect of extra student neurons.
Training degradation in deep plain networks and prevention through identity shortcuts or special initialization.
Initialization effects on signal propagation, learning speed and trainable depth.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, curvature dynamics, recovery and divergence.
BN versus no normalization for accuracy gain and learning-rate tolerance; Fixup training without normalization.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the V1 limits_scope verdict: an unspecified classification-error measure and untested conditions do not establish a limitation of V1. GAN training speed, normalization runtime and whitening instability do not test initialization, learning-rate thresholds or BN versus no normalization.

versions.untested_parts: Random labels, CIFAR-100 class-conditional generation, model width, early stopping, and whether reported classification error is training error are not tested or specified.
